extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of constitutional theory; statesmen, lawmakers, and political theorists
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for constitutions and the structure of government, arguing for separation of powers and checks (executive, senate, representatives) to protect minority rights, property, and liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer a mixed constitution to a single sovereign assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: A mixed government (composition of monarchial, aristocratical, and popular elements) is superior to a single sovereign assembly because it prevents degeneration into an oligarchy or tyranny and balances competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author repeatedly contrasts a mixed government with a 'single assembly' or 'single sovereign assembly' and argues that a mixture of executive, senate (aristocratical), and people (representatives) avoids the concentration of all power in one centre and the consequent rapid slide into revolution or tyranny. Avoid 'jumbling all these powers in one centre.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an independent senate to protect property and check the people
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent senate is necessary as an 'effectual barrier in the constitution against being robbed, plundered, and murdered' for the rich and to balance the representatives who guard the poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues the rich need an independent senate and the poor need a house of representatives; both are required to secure equal justice. The senate must be sufficiently independent (in tenure/power) to resist transient popular passions and protect property rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: House of representatives as essential branch representing the people
rubrics_metrics.description: The people's 'fair, full, and honest consent' through representatives must be an essential part of the constitution; the people should have an absolute control over grants of money and a negative on laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The people (via their representatives) should retain essential legislative powers—particularly financial control and the right to accuse/enforce—while their powers should be limited so they do not exercise executive or judicial functions. Representation must be 'full and just' and not a mere pretense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive with a negative (veto) equal to other branches
rubrics_metrics.description: An executive power vested with a negative, equal to either house, is necessary to hold the balance between rich and poor and to decide when they cannot agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though the negative 'may be used perhaps never,' its known existence prevents abuses and has historically prevented constitutional overturns (England example). The negative is a deterrent; absence of such a power will be felt daily and lead to instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers and executive officers must be accountable and impeachable
rubrics_metrics.description: In a mixed government, ministers (at least of the executive power) should be responsible for every instance of exercise of power and, if corrupted, be accountable to a house of representatives and amenable to impeachment and trial before independent judges and a senate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This accountability chain (representatives -> impeachment -> senate trial -> independent judges) is presented as a safeguard against corruption and abuse of executive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not consolidate legislative, executive, and judicial powers in the people or one assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving the people, collectively or by representation, the executive and judicial power, or the whole uncontrollable legislative power, corrupts them and throws whole power into hands of the most profligate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author warns that when one body holds all powers, the vicious and unprincipled will form majority coalitions and plunder the rich or fleece the poor; separation of powers is necessary to avoid such abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect minorities from tyranny of the majority (negative for minority)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no possible way of defending the minority in a single sovereign assembly from the tyranny of the majority except by giving the minority a negative (veto), though the liberrum veto is cited as an absurd and ruinous extreme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains the danger of majorities being accountable only to their own constituents and thus rewarding themselves; a properly balanced negative is necessary to protect minority rights without the ruinous consequences of absolute unanimous vetoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid too-frequent rotation in office—longer tenure mitigates faction
rubrics_metrics.description: Short annual elections for supreme magistrates or senators invite faction, party, bribery, and the quick accumulation of popular influence; prolonging duration of office (longer terms, life, or hereditary) may mitigate these ills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that longer periods lessen and postpone the evils of factionalism and that rapid annual rotation leads to instability and the eventual rise of a despot. He admits hereditary tenure is an extreme remedy but argues the alternatives (longer terms) are worth considering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws and taxes must be by common consent and common to all
rubrics_metrics.description: A fundamental law should require that no load (tax/burden) be laid on any but what is common to all, and always by common consent; not to serve the lusts of any but only to supply the necessities of the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional design must prevent special burdens or taxes targeted at particular groups; equality before taxation and law is emphasized as a constitutional principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plain, precise language and reasoning in constitutional discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry and mystic flourish 'will answer no good end' in discussing constitutions; the simplest style and 'the most mathematical precision of words and ideas' is best adapted to discover and convey truth on these questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a meta-guideline for how to argue about constitutional design—favor clarity, precision, and avoidance of rhetorical flourish intended to mislead or amuse the populace without informing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power will be abused when unlimited and unbalanced, whether permanent or temporary
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not permanency but omnipotence — being unlimited, unbalanced, uncontrouled — that occasions abuse. Temporary authority can be worse because it is often abused to secure revival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design checks and balances to limit power and prevent omnipotence. Do not assume that temporariness alone prevents corruption; structure and limits matter more than tenure alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent parties, factions, bribes, and armies from deciding affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: If parties, factions, drunkenness, bribes, armies, and delirium come in, elections and popular government fail; constitutional design should avoid structures that make the system vulnerable to these forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical safeguards (longer terms, balanced branches, independent magistrates) are offered as methods to reduce susceptibility to factional capture and demagoguery; otherwise recourse to conventions and extraordinary measures will be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against representatives being merely instruments of the great and rich
rubrics_metrics.description: If representatives are constituted in a way that leaves them open to influence by great and rich persons, equal laws cannot be expected; in a single assembly the great will govern via influence and the poor by numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutional independence for representatives and complementary branches (senate/executive) so that neither influence nor numerical tyranny can routinely prevail to the detriment of equality and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure an impartial tribunal and independent judges for trials of public officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Accused ministers and magistrates should be tried and punished before independent judges; independent judiciary is essential to render impeachment and punishment effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The accountability mechanism described requires impartial adjudication distinct from legislative or executive control; judicial independence is thus a constitutional requirement for enforcing standards of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit popular power over private property
rubrics_metrics.description: The people should not have the power to take from one man his property to make another easy; popular remedies must not include confiscatory or unequal laws against property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect property rights constitutionally by preventing majorities from enacting unequal laws that transfer property among citizens; balance popular grievance redress with protections for individual rights.
